findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — [P1, confidence 100] `return response` exposes either a native Fetch Response, a Gaxios response, or an already-decoded HubSpot token from the same `() => any` boundary, so credential-sync mode deterministically violates the Google caller's `.data` contract and the HubSpot caller's token-object contract instead of providing one integration-independent refresh result.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — [P1, confidence 100] `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and the same computed key on line 10 create a literal object key rather than a dynamic numeric-field rule, so Zod strips the real expiry property from sync responses and persisted credentials remain expired, forcing refresh on every operation.

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — [P1, confidence 100] `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` changes an absent refresh token from “retain the existing secret” to a fabricated credential, and the Office 365 merge at `CalendarService.ts:264` overwrites the valid token so the next refresh is permanently rejected.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — [P1, confidence 100] `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` followed by `data: { key }` persists Zod's `{ success, data }` result wrapper instead of the credential object, so the next service construction rejects the stored row against `googleCredentialSchema`.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:90 — [P1, confidence 100] `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)` selects the minimal sync schema whenever sharing is enabled even though line 75 still calls Salesforce directly, so it strips `instance_url` from the persisted credential and the next connection is built without its required instance endpoint.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — [P2, confidence 75] `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` gives the webhook no unique credential identity, so users with multiple credentials for one app have an arbitrary row updated while the credential selected by normal reads remains stale.

docs/tasks/task-001.md:2 — P1, confidence 100: `Review the change.` supplies no acceptance criteria for provider coverage, webhook create/update semantics, configuration, failure behavior, or verification, so task-done cannot establish that OAuth credential sync satisfies its stated intent.

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:72 — P1, confidence 100: `if (appCredential)` adds credential update and create branches without any test or spec change in HEAD~2..HEAD, so CI accepts a webhook that writes the wrong credential or fails one of the two persistence paths.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the webhook endpoint at line 62 uses `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` which will return an arbitrary credential when a user has multiple credentials for the same app. The code then updates this arbitrary credential at lines 69-77, or creates a new one at lines 79-86. This is a real bug because: 1) Users can have multiple credentials for the same app (e.g., multiple Google Calendar accounts), 2) The webhook has no way to specify which credential to update, 3) findFirst returns an arbitrary matching row, so the wrong credential could be updated while the intended one remains stale. This is a correctness issue in the new webhook endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts, line 100 shows `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then line 101-103 shows `await prisma.credential.update({ where: { id: credential.id }, data: { key }, });`. The parseRefreshTokenResponse function (shown in the diff at packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts) returns the result of `schema.safeParse(response)`, which is an object like `{ success: boolean, data: ... }`. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — P1, confidence 100: `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(` receives a Fetch `Response` on the sync path instead of a `HubspotToken`, so expiry calculation and token installation use missing fields while the catch logs and suppresses the failed refresh.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts, the code wraps the hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken call with refreshOAuthTokens(). The refreshOAuthTokens function (in packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) returns either a fetch Response object (when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set) or the result of refreshFunction(). When credential sync is enabled, it returns a raw fetch Response, not the HubspotToken that the code expects.
